item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00049","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C05","C04","C08"],"selected_candidate_label":"C05","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C05 is the specific March 23 directive expressly identified by the child as creating the Board of Inquiry whose report triggered the next statutory step. The child repeats C05's identification of the parties and its distinctive finding that the coal strike affects a substantial part of an industry engaged in interstate and foreign commerce and in producing goods for commerce, and that continuation will imperil national health and safety. It then uses the board report produced under C05 to direct the Attorney General to seek an injunction. C04 and C08 employ closely parallel Labor Management Relations Act board-of-inquiry machinery, but concern other disputes and are weaker templates than the expressly incorporated C05.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"On March 23, 1948 ... I issued [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], creating a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues involved in a labor dispute between coal operators and associations signatory to the National Bituminous Coal Wage Agreement of 1947 and certain of their employees represented by the International Union, United Mine Workers of America","parent_excerpt":"WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute between coal operators and associations signatory to the National Bituminous Coal Wage Agreement of 1947 and certain of their employees represented by the International Union, United Mine Workers of America","explanation":"The child expressly invokes C05 and repeats its detailed identification of the dispute and parties."},{"child_excerpt":"this unresolved labor dispute has resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade and commerce among the several States and with foreign nations, and in the production of goods for commerce, which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety","parent_excerpt":"such dispute has resulted in a strike affecting a substantial part of the bituminous coal industry, an industry engaged in trade and commerce among the several states and with foreign nations, and in the production of goods for commerce, which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national health and safety","explanation":"This is substantial near-verbatim reuse of C05's industry, commerce, and national-emergency finding."},{"child_excerpt":"On March 31, 1948, I received the Board's written report ... I therefore direct you ... to petition ... any district court ... to enjoin the continuance of such strike","parent_excerpt":"The Board shall report to the President in accordance with provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before April 5, 1948.","explanation":"The child continues the same statutory administrative sequence: C05 establishes the inquiry and report, while the child acts on that report by initiating the injunction stage."}]}
